bullets.title: META's 2027 AI Capex Eyeing $250-275B, Doubling Compute to 14GW
bullets.body: Multiple sources converge on META planning to double compute capacity from 7GW to 14GW by end-2027, implying capex of $200-275B vs. Morgan Stanley's prior $175B model. META's first large-scale multi-GW Prometheus cluster came online in July; capacity constraints are broadening from GPUs to CPU, memory, and disk. META also secured multi-year supply deals with Samsung, SK Hynix, and Sumitomo, and is launching proprietary 'Iris' AI chip in September via AVGO partnership with TSMC manufacturing.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Equipment Bull Case Strengthens; WFE Estimates Raised to $185-200B in CY27
bullets.body: Citi models 2026/27/28 WFE at $145B/$200B/$250B; Mizuho raises CY27 WFE to $192B (+25% YoY) and CY28 to $221B on META's 14GW plan and hyperscaler spend acceleration. TSMC raised 2026 capex to high end of $52-56B with Citi modeling $75B/$80B in 2027/28; Samsung announced $1.36T investment through 2040; Micron raised FY26 net capex to $27B+ and FY27 to $45B+. Mizuho raises AMAT PT to $650 (from $540) and LRCX PT to $400; Wolfe favors AMAT for DRAM exposure and flags ASML as nearer-term catalyst.

bullets.title: AVGO Signs >$30B Multiyear Deal with Apple; Custom AI Silicon Ramp Seen 2029/30
bullets.body: Broadcom announces >$30B multiyear agreement with Apple covering custom silicon and wireless connectivity, including $1.5B capex upgrade at Fort Collins and >15B U.S.-made chips—Apple's largest American Manufacturing Program commitment. Analysts view the deal as securing AVGO's RF component position and expanding its ASIC role beyond prior 5G agreement; Citi expects a notable custom AI silicon ramp around 2029/30. AVGO shares +4.8% on the announcement.

bullets.title: AI Capex Cycle Broadly Intact; $700B Hyperscaler Spend Estimate May Be Conservative
bullets.body: Jefferies (Brent Thill) and multiple buy-side sources argue META's capex trajectory signals the AI buildout is in early innings, with $700B hyperscaler capex potentially conservative. AMZN's Moonraker project is budgeting $100M+ in GPU costs in 2026 despite Trainium ramp; NVDA GB200/300 rack output tracking 70-80K racks in CY26 (100%+ YoY). Ken Griffin flagged compute capacity and energy infrastructure as the central constraint on AI deployment.

bullets.title: CIO Survey: IT Budgets Accelerating to +3.3% YoY; AI Now #1 Priority Ahead of Cybersecurity
bullets.body: Citi's CIO survey shows IT budgets growing at +3.3% YoY (vs. +2.6% prior), above the 7-year average, with AI moving to the top spending priority ahead of cybersecurity. MSFT, AMZN, and GOOGL screen best for AI spend increases; CRWD and PANW lead in cybersecurity. Tyler Radke's new top software picks are MDB, SNOW, and PLTR for data infrastructure/AI enablement.

bullets.title: Enterprise Token Optimization Wave: Firms Capping AI Spend, Routing to Cheaper/Open-Source Models
bullets.body: After 8-12x daily token volume growth from Jan-May, tech firms are now capping AI usage and routing workloads to lower-cost or open-source models, with enterprise success shifting to business outcomes over token consumption. Chinese open-source models (DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen) gaining adoption in US enterprise; Beijing reconsidering its pro-open-source stance. This 'Tokenmaxx trend reversal' could reshape the AI investment narrative in 2H26 and threatens legacy software vendors.

bullets.title: AI Model Pricing War Intensifies; SpaceX Grok 4.5 at $2/$6 vs OpenAI $5/$30
bullets.body: SpaceX's Grok 4.5 launched at $2/$6 per million input/output tokens, significantly undercutting OpenAI's GPT at $5/$30; META's Muse Spark 1.1 priced at $1.25/$4.25. Zuckerberg flagged competing labs' pricing as having 'very high margins,' signaling a concerted push by META, SpaceX, and Chinese model companies toward cheaper frontier-class performance. OpenAI claims GPT 5.6 is 54% more token efficient on agentic coding tasks.

bullets.title: Micron Raises U.S. Capex to >$250B Through 2035; Commits $3B to Domestic Supply Chain
bullets.body: Micron increased its U.S. fab investment target to >$250B through 2035 (from $200B), targeting 40% of DRAM production domestically. The company also announced a $3B strategic investment in the U.S. semiconductor ecosystem including $500M financing to GlobalWafers for a Texas 300mm wafer fab plus a 10-year supply agreement.

bullets.title: Taiwan June Exports +40.3% YoY, Missed 49.9% Consensus; ICT Near-Record on AI Demand
bullets.body: Taiwan June export growth came in at 40.3% YoY, missing the 49.9% consensus and down 1.1% MoM seasonally adjusted, though ICT product exports jumped +5.6% MoM to near-record $35B, up 7-fold from 2023 lows. Taiwan imports hit an all-time high, signaling robust AI supply chain activity; the TAIEX is near all-time highs, outperforming MSCI World and S&P since 'Liberation Day.'

bullets.title: ECB June Rate Hike Was 'Clear-Cut'; Further Hikes Embedded in Baseline
bullets.body: ECB June minutes show the 25bp hike was viewed internally as very clear-cut with minimal counter-arguments; mild scenario projections include almost three hikes and show core inflation above target through end-2028. The council explicitly rejected characterizing the move as precautionary; energy prices lower since June reduce some upside inflation risk but further hikes remain in the baseline despite non-committal forward guidance.

bullets.title: Initial Jobless Claims Edge Down to 215K; Labor Market Steady
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims fell 2K WoW to 215K, with the 4-week average at 219K, past the peak of residual seasonality that had boosted summer headlines. Continuing claims are moving sideways, consistent with a steady re-hire rate; UBS notes the data supports preference for PAYC over temp staffing names like EFOR and RHI.

bullets.title: June Existing Home Sales Miss at 4.09M (-2.4% MoM); Market Remains Range-Bound
bullets.body: June existing home sales fell 2.4% MoM to 4.09M, below consensus expectations for a small uptick, with breadth mostly negative except the Northeast. YTD average of 4.08M is in-line with 2025 levels; strategists expect sales to end the year flat. Median prices rose 1.8% YoY (accelerating from 1.4% in June 2025), while affordability improved modestly on stronger income growth.

bullets.title: NDX at ~23x NTM P/E, Inline with 10-Year Average; Momentum Healing Post-Drawdown
bullets.body: GS notes NDX is trading at ~23x NTM P/E, inline with the 10-year average and toward the lower end of the 3-4 year range. Momentum pairs closed up 3-4% yesterday after 25-30% pullbacks; VIX at 16.29 (-3.6%) with S&P 500 +0.5% to 7,522. ANET and NET hit new 52-week highs (+78.7% and +41.9% respectively over 52 weeks).

bullets.title: META $13B Alberta Data Center (1GW) Signals Hyperscaler Infrastructure Push Into Canada
bullets.body: META unveiled a $13B, 1GW data center in Sturgeon County, Alberta—its first in Canada and largest outside the US—with a $4.6B, 932MW gas-fired power plant being built by Pembina and Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners. The Canadian government cites 20GW of planned data center capacity vs. 337MW currently in operation; Alberta targeting $100B in data center investment by 2030.

bullets.title: German Manufacturing Stabilizes; May Exports Surge 23% to U.S. Ahead of Potential Tariffs
bullets.body: German May exports unexpectedly rose, approaching 2022 record highs, with U.S.-bound shipments up +23.1% MoM, likely front-running tariff increases. EU factory orders jumped +11.2% MoM; however, German GDP is modeled at only ~1% growth in 2026/early 2027, and structural headwinds persist (energy dependency, weak autos, China competition). DAX at record highs supported by energy, tech, and banks.

bullets.title: KOSPI at 20-Year Record Low Valuation; SOX at 4% Discount to SPX
bullets.body: KOSPI is trading at a 20-year record low 6x NTM P/E per Morgan Stanley; the SOX semiconductor index trades at a 4% discount to the S&P 500 on 2-year forward P/E. Memory stocks remain wobbly near-term from quant/ETF flows, but are liked long-term; Samsung ADR issuance expected end of week could serve as an inflection point.

bullets.title: Hotels RevPAR +10.9% YoY Week Ended 7/4 on World Cup Boost; Urban Markets +23%
bullets.body: U.S. hotel RevPAR surged +10.9% YoY for the week ended July 4th, with World Cup host markets seeing extreme outperformance: Philadelphia +39%, Washington DC +57%. Preliminary June RevPAR tracking +8-9% YoY; urban market RevPAR +23.0%, group +13.5%, transient +13.0%.

bullets.title: P&C Insurance Soft Cycle Could Last ~Decade; Life Insurance Upside on Rate Hike Pivot
bullets.body: Wolfe Research's insurance preview flags an elongated P&C soft pricing cycle potentially lasting nearly a decade, with MGAs and reinsurers adding to capital oversupply. Life insurance stocks seen as beneficiaries of any rate hike pivot; reinsurer returns expected to converge with cost of capital only by 2027E. Broker data center revenue opportunity viewed as overhyped.

bullets.title: June Dodge Momentum Index Slows to +1.9% MoM; Data Center Pace Moderates
bullets.body: The June Dodge Momentum Index decelerated to +1.9% MoM (vs. +5.9% in May), with commercial buildings down 6.8% MoM and data center activity moderating from elevated recent levels. Institutional building rose +10.9% MoM; planning activity accelerated across nearly every other sector despite the June pullback.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO and Capital Markets Reopening Signal; Alt Managers See Q2 Lighter Realizations
bullets.body: Citizens views the SpaceX IPO as a fee event and confidence signal for capital markets reopening, expecting strong Q2 results from GS and MS on healthy trading and capital markets. Alternative managers are benefiting from secular growth tailwinds but Q2 realizations expected to be lighter; alt stocks have underperformed traditional managers by 55% over the past year despite net inflows.
